answer: A chain of verifiable delay functions can blunt Sybils: each identity must complete a sequential puzzle seeded by the prior epoch, taking real minutes that cannot be parallelized, before its work counts. Like a tide that rises only at its own pace, no burst of fake accounts reaches the zenith faster; an attacker facing a gale of new identities still pays full serial time per identity, so mass creation costs as much as it gains, while one honest agent pays once.
